transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2026-09-28 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 52 mins
- Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood CSM), Daniel (CarbonScale Head of ML), Aisha (SRE), Liam (Lead Infra), Sofia (Product)

Auto-summary: mid-POC check-in; focus on TTFT instability spikes and streaming path microbursts, plan for seqlen sweep and kernel A/B.

00:00 Jordan (AE): all right folks, thanks for making time, uh we'll kick off, quick agenda — run through last week's numbers, dig into the p95/p99 on first token, and then decide kernel toggles and what traces we need.
00:18 Daniel (Head of ML): yeah thanks, we saw those big spikes yesterday evening, like 300 to 900 ms jumps, it made our chat UI stutter.
00:28 Priya (SE): mm-hmm, and to be clear, are those on hosted redwood or your dedicated pilot nodes?
00:33 Liam (Lead Infra): it's the dedicated pool we've been testing — the ones with the 8xA10g profiles. We did enable prefix cache for sessions, but there were some cold-starts.
00:42 Priya (SE): ok, that tracks. cold KV cache can cause a 200–400ms delta on first tokens, but the microbursts to 900 suggest either kernel jitter or scheduler coalescing under microburst load.
00:55 Aisha (SRE): we also noticed spikes correlated with other batch jobs at ~02:00 UTC — could be noisy neighbor on the infra env, maybe our autoscaling policy is too slow.
01:08 Jordan (AE): quick clarifying q — are those other jobs on the same host group or same rack?
01:12 Liam: same rack, different tenancy — but it's the dedicated pool we reserved, shouldn't be noisy neighbors like cloud public tenancy. there may be background maintenance IO.
01:22 Priya (SE): got it. From Redwood's side, we looked at kernel logs — there's a case where the fused-attention kernel falls back to the generic matmul path when seqlen crosses 768 for certain batch shapes, that triggers a runtime switch and higher latency.
01:36 Daniel: so the model is a 13B that does dynamic routing, sequences swing from 64 up to 1024 in production. we set max seqlen to 1024 in the pilot.
01:46 Priya: yep, that range explains it. fused kernels are optimal up to ~768 for our build; beyond that it uses a different execution path. switching at runtime can cost ~150–300ms on the first token after the switch while caches warm.
02:05 Sofia (Product): is there an option to force one kernel path so we don't pay the swing cost?
02:08 Priya: you can pin kernel selection per model variant. tradeoff: forcing fused kernel past its sweet spot can increase token latency overall due to less efficient math, and may blow up GPU memory. forcing generic kernel for all lengths is more stable but slightly higher baseline.
02:24 Daniel: hmm ok, stability > tiny baseline improvement — I think product will prefer predictability.
02:29 Jordan: noted. Jordan to follow up with kernel decision matrix + tradeoff numbers.
02:34 Maya (CSM): we should also capture traces at the precise jump times — p99 and p999 — to understand if it's a scheduler or kernel issue.
02:41 Aisha: we can run trace collection during the 02:00 maintenance window, will that help?
02:46 Priya: yes, please capture full perf traces with KV cache both on and off. also include the runtime logs that show the kernel selection decision and the env variables for quantization path.
03:00 Daniel: quick question on streaming — we see partial tokens delayed mid-stream, not just first token. like the early stream is fine but at 200–350ms steps we lose packets or get pauses.
03:12 Priya: streaming pauses can be due to our chunking logic and small microbursts causing the process to switch from continuous batching to single-request mode. That happens when queue depth drops and the runtime flushes a half-batch.
03:28 Daniel: are there tunables to reduce the flush sensitivity?
03:31 Priya: yes, the streaming threshold and flush timer are tunables. increasing the small-batch window will smooth streaming but raises median latency slightly. you can also enable hedging where the system sends early partials from a cheaper model variant and replaces them when full result arrives — that's more complex.
03:48 Liam: we were curious about hedging — sounds like an interesting fallback. Any pitfalls?
03:52 Priya: hedging adds extra token compute cost and can complicate consistency. it helps when you have a cheaper local small model to seed early tokens and then get the final from remote. If you don't have a cheap local model, hedging is just duplicate work.
04:06 Daniel: we do have a 2B smaller variant for on-device experiments, could be used for hedging early tokens.
04:11 Jordan: ok good note. Jordan to include cost delta analysis for hedging with 2B local + remote final.
04:17 Aisha: security question — if we enable KV cache sharing across sessions for perf, does that expose sensitive context? we need to make sure caching respects session boundaries and encryption.
04:26 Priya: Redwood supports per-customer KMS + HSM integration on private deployments; KV cache is pinned per session by default. If you want shared prefixes, we can do tokenized hash boundaries but we avoid sharing raw context. We'll share the security brief.
04:38 Aisha: please do. We need SOC2 + encryption notes before moving to dedicated in prod.
04:45 Jordan: will send SOC2 + architecture notes.
04:48 Priya: back to traces — ideally we get three sets: seqlen 64-256, 257-768, 769-1024; each with prefix cache on/off, and with streaming enabled/disabled. That matrix will let us see kernel transitions.
05:05 Daniel: we'll run that. we can target 1k requests per bucket over 24 hours to get p95/p99.
05:12 Priya: perfect. Also please include the exact input token distribution — sometimes model prompts with very long system messages shift the distribution and we see different batching profiles.
05:22 Sofia: there's also a new front-end change that will add more system context; I'll flag that as a variable.
05:27 Jordan: ok, let's talk timeline: do the traces by next Monday (2026-10-05), Priya to analyze by Wednesday and propose kernel pinning + hedging decision, then we do a follow-up the week after.
05:38 Daniel: sounds good.
05:40 Priya: one more misc item — we saw GPU hiccups around memory compaction on a couple hosts; we'll capture dmesg and driver logs when you run the sweeps.
05:52 Aisha: will do, and if we see host-level noise we'll swap instances during the night run.
06:00 Jordan: ok final recap — action items and next steps are in the notes. Anything else?
06:05 Daniel: can you also share the microburst spreadsheet you mentioned last week?
06:09 Jordan: yes, sending after this meeting along with the kernel decision doc.
06:12 Maya: I'll get a 30-min follow-up on the calendar for 2026-10-07 to review results.
06:18 Daniel: thanks everyone.
06:20 (end)

Notes about transcript: occasional recognition errors — "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "K-V cash" and "fused kernels" as "fuse kernels". There's mild crosstalk during the early troubleshooting discussion.
